world: THE WORLD: Eliet is a small village in a wide, cold valley ringed by hills and mountains (think Morrowind and Skyrim, with an eastern cultivation soul). Under Eliet a dungeon goes down floor after floor; deep below are settlements built in the dark: Shellhaven (on the back of a sleeping tortoise), Lanternmere, Ironroot Hold, the Jade Pagoda. Long ago something seeded the world with NANITES -- microscopic machines that live in blood and stone. Cultivators refine qi and tune their nanites together: each realm of cultivation has a nanite stage -- Body Tempering / Nanite Seeding, Qi Condensation / Nanite Bloom, Foundation Establishment / Nanite Lattice, Core Formation / Nanite Core, Nascent Soul / Nanite Ascendance, Soul Transformation / Nanite Transcendence. The five elements (wood, fire, earth, metal, water) feed and overcome each other. The Lotus Ascent Academy takes only those who pass its entrance exam. The dungeon is the main road to power, but not the only one: out in the valley stand ancient TOWERS to climb and SECTS in the hills that take disciples. Tone: grounded, weathered, a little eerie; people are practical, poor, proud.

briefs.ask: One cultivation sect that lives out in the valley, outside the dungeon -- a place a cultivator can join, train with, and rise in. Each sect must feel different: its element, where it sits, what it believes, how it treats the nanites in its disciples' blood, how you get in, three arts it teaches (one attack, one defence, one movement), its elder, and who it quarrels with.

briefs.title: The great bloodlines
briefs.ask: One of the ten great bloodlines that can wake in a cultivator's veins deep in the dungeon. Write the one for this item number, in this order (set "line" to its key exactly): 1. azure_dragon -- the east wind's dragon; qi gathers in its blood like rain; 2. vermilion_phoenix -- the south's undying bird; its blood refuses endings (rises from a killing blow); 3. white_tiger -- the west's killing star; finds the gap in any armour; 4. black_tortoise -- the north's patient shell; blows land lighter; 5. qilin -- the benevolent beast; fortune and plenty follow it; 6. nine_tailed_fox -- a trickster's blood, hard to catch; blows meet only where it was; 7. golden_crow -- the three-legged bird that carries the sun; its touch burns; 8. kunpeng -- the great fish that became the great bird; it wants distance and speed; 9. asura -- war-blood; the nearer to falling, the harder it strikes; 10. starborn_lattice -- not a beast at all -- nanites folded into a family line generations ago, remembering. Write it from inside the world: what people call it (a name of a few words), what it is and where the old families who carry it came from, the first small physical sign it gives someone when it stirs, and what its power feels like once it is half awake. briefs.title: The daily trial's twists
briefs.ask: One of the eight twists the trial-keeper in Eliet can post on the daily trial, in this order (set "twist" to its key exactly): 1. blood_moon -- elites everywhere, and they carry more; 2. glass_edge -- every blow lands half again as hard, yours and theirs; 3. swarming -- half as many again of them, each a little weaker; 4. ironhide -- tough hides, rich pickings; 5. quickened -- they move faster than they should; 6. spirit_tide -- the air thick with qi: twice what you'd gather; 7. no_mercy -- your wounds don't close on their own in there; 8. veteran -- every foe has a fighting style, no plain brawlers. Give it the name it's known by on the Trial Board (two or three words) and one line, in the keeper's dry voice, warning what it means for whoever goes in. Keep what it does.

briefs.title: Rare happenings in the deep
briefs.ask: One of the six rare happenings that can take a floor of the dungeon for a day, in this order (set "event" to its key exactly): 1. blood_moon -- the light down there goes red; more of them, and worse; 2. spirit_tide -- qi rolls through the halls like a spring flood; 3. wandering_master -- an old cultivator camped on a floor, passing through, who'll talk for a fee; 4. meteor_fall -- something fell through the rock and still glows: star iron for the quick; 5. treasure_spirit -- a gilded little thing running about dropping coins, gone within minutes; 6. heavenly_sign -- the stars show through the rock for a moment and old blood answers. Give it the name the people of Eliet use for it (two or three words) and the line a cultivator thinks, arriving on that floor and seeing it. Keep what it does.

example.desc: what you see and feel, arriving: one or two sentences

briefs.title: The story: thirteen acts
briefs.ask: One act of the main story, in this order (set "act" to its key exactly): 1. seeding -- What the Deep Put in You (Elder Mo; choices: 'The village should know the truth.' / 'Keep it between us. People sleep better.') 2. first_master -- The Keeper's Keys (Smith Hale; choices: 'The village gets its share.' / 'I earned it. I keep it.') 3. wens_debt -- What the Mine Remembers (Trader Wen; choices: 'Clear Wen's debt (200 gold).' / 'That's your debt, Wen.') 4. envoy -- The Sects Take Notice (Elder Mo; choices: 'I'll go to the hills and choose.' / 'Eliet is my sect.') 5. blood -- What Runs in You (Apothecary Lin; choices: 'Draw it.' / 'No. It's mine.') 6. rival -- The One Who Counts Your Wins (Captain Rhee; choices: 'Let him come.' / 'Send word. I've nothing to prove.') 7. pagoda -- The Elder's Confession (Elder Mo; choices: 'I forgive you. You brought back what saved us.' / 'You should have told us.') 8. mirror -- The Mirror (Elder Mo; choices: 'Seal the shaft. Eliet comes first.' / 'I go on. The deep isn't finished with me.') 9. expedition -- The Lodge Goes Down (Captain Rhee; choices: 'I'll lead them. Pick your six.' / 'Keep them home. The deep is mine to carry.') 10. last_steel -- The Last Steel (Smith Hale; choices: 'Through the night, then. Let's make it.' / 'Finish it your way. briefs.title: The lever tablets
briefs.ask: A worn stone tablet beside three coloured levers on a dungeon floor, telling whoever reads it the order to pull them -- but as a riddle, a rhyme, a maker's rule, a fragment of an old song: never a bare list. The three colours go in as %s, %s, %s in the order they must be pulled (exactly three %s, in order). Two to four sentences. Different each time: a mason's note, a child's rhyme, a warning, a prayer, a ledger.

example.text: Three hands turned the stone. %s first, who dug it. Then %s, who shored it. %s last, who sealed it.

briefs.title: The road down: twelve chapters
briefs.ask: One chapter of the main quest, in this order (set "chapter" to its key exactly): 1. first_steps -- ours: "The Road Down" -- Elder Mo wants to see what the deep makes of you. Talk to him, go down to the first floor, and come back with the goblin chief's head.; 2. three_floors -- ours: "What the Mine Keeps" -- Three floors, a salve of your own making, and the third floor's master. The deep teaches by being new; so does the bench.; 3. condense -- ours: "Condense" -- The air below the fifth floor drowns an untempered body. Fill your sea of qi, open your ring, face the heart demon: Qi Condensation. Then the way down to six opens.; 4. deep_breath -- ours: "Deep Breath" -- Past the tenth floor the air sits in the lungs like water. Apothecary Lin knows the pill the old miners took -- learn alchemy enough to brew it yourself.; 5. foundation -- ours: "Nascent" -- Fifteen floors down there is a town, and below it something that reaches for the unwarded. Grow a nascent soul, join a guild, and cut a ward of jade and silver.; 6. blood_and_dark -- ours: "Blood and Dark" -- Twenty floors: the Jade Pagoda, and the blood waking in you. Below it, a dark that torches don't answer. Survival will carry you; stormglass will light you.; 7. core -- ours: "Body and Qi as One" -- The twenty-fifth floor's master wears your face. Integrate body and qi, kill it, and decide what you are -- the deep won't take anyone who hasn't.; 8. thin_air -- ours: "Thin Air" -- Below thirty the qi turns thin and ordinary blood sickens. The Lodge is going down behind you; Lin's voidsalt will keep you alive ahead of them. Make your home somewhere worth coming back to.; 9. nascent -- ours: "Tribulation" -- Thirty-six is cold enough to still a lesser soul. Pass your tribulation, master a weapon as your own hand, put heartfire in your chest, and stand with Hale through the night at the forge.; 10. star_iron_door -- ours: "The Star Iron Door" -- Forty floors, and the children of Eliet dream the deep. A door of star iron waits on forty-one, locked by the first expedition. Answer Lin, then forge the key.; 11. the_letter -- ours: "Knock Politely" -- Forty-five: a wall with a merchant's seal. Open Wen's letter with him, climb the immortal realms, and bind a ward of the Heart's own silver.; 12. the_heart -- ours: "The Heart of the Deep" -- Fifty floors. The Heart of the Deep, and whatever it is you've become. Kill its master and walk in.. Keep what the chapter asks of the player (the goals are fixed); give it a better name (two to five words) and a brief: two or three sentences in the voice of the townsperson who sets it, telling the player where to go and why.

example.brief: two or three sentences, the elder's voice

briefs.title: The gates down
briefs.ask: What the player reads when the stairs to a gated floor turn them back, in this order (set "floor" exactly): 1. floor 6 -- ours: "Below the fifth floor the qi is thick enough to drown in. A body that hasn't condensed it can't breathe it."; 2. floor 11 -- ours: "The air past the tenth floor is wrong -- it sits in the lungs like water. Only stormglass holds a light down there, and only the seasoned keep their feet."; 5. floor 26 -- ours: "Past the Mirror nothing is mapped. The deep won't take a cultivator whose body and qi aren't one -- or one who hasn't decided what they are."; 6. floor 31 -- ours: "Below thirty the qi turns thin and strange, and ordinary blood sickens in a day. briefs.title: Who are you? (character creation)
briefs.ask: One of the seven questions asked when a new player makes their character, in this order (set "id" exactly): 1. born -- ours: "Where were you born?" -- answers: "In Eliet, in sight of the shaft." / "In the hills, among the herders." / "Under a sect's roof, a servant's child." / "On the road -- never two nights in the same place."; 2. trouble -- ours: "When trouble came to your door, what did you do?" -- answers: "Stood in front of the others." / "Hit first, and hardest." / "I was already round the back." / "Talked until it went away."; 3. hands -- ours: "What did your hands do most, growing up?" -- answers: "Carried, dug and hauled." / "Quick work: knots, locks, other people's pockets." / "Very little. I sat, and listened, and breathed." / "A bit of everything, none of it well."; 4. fear -- ours: "What do you fear most?" -- answers: "Being weak when it matters." / "Being caught." / "Being forgotten." / "Being alone."; 5. why -- ours: "Why are you going down the shaft?" -- answers: "For Eliet. Someone has to." / "For power. I'm tired of being small." / "For the truth of what's down there." / "Someone I loved went down and didn't come back."; 6. temper -- ours: "Which is most like you?" -- answers: "Patient. I can wait out anything." / "Fierce. I don't back down." / "Careful. I check twice." / "Restless. I'm already moving."; 7. road -- ours: "How much of who you are will you leave to the road?" -- answers: "Nothing. I know exactly who I am." / "A little. I know mostly." / "All of it. The road will tell me.". Keep what each answer MEANS (the game weighs them: the answer about standing in front makes them sturdier, the one about hitting first stronger, and so on) and keep the same number of answers in the same order. Write the question as someone in Eliet would ask it, and each answer short, first person.

briefs.title: Rune words
briefs.ask: A rune word is runes set in the right order on one piece: they run together and speak, and give more than their sum. Old Oda tells the player one at a time, as a riddle-ish hint. Name each word and write Oda's hint, in this order (set "id" exactly): 1. keen_flame -- ours: "Keen Flame" -- Edge then Ember on weapon -- hint: "Edge, then Ember, on a blade."; 2. gale_edge -- ours: "Gale Edge" -- Wind then Edge on weapon -- hint: "The wind first, and the cut it carries."; 3. rooted_oak -- ours: "Rooted Oak" -- Root then Stone on wear -- hint: "Root into stone, on something you wear."; 4. stillwater -- ours: "Stillwater" -- Tide then Stone on wear -- hint: "The tide that meets a stone and stops."; 5. seers_mark -- ours: "Seer's Mark" -- Eye then Fortune on any -- hint: "An eye for fortune, anywhere you carry it."; 6. heartfire -- ours: "Heartfire" -- Ember then Root then Ember on weapon -- hint: "A root between two embers."; 7. thunderclap -- ours: "Thunderclap" -- Storm then Storm then Edge on weapon -- hint: "Storm, storm, and then the edge comes down."; 8. singing_blade -- ours: "Singing Blade" -- Song then Wind then Song on weapon -- hint: "Two songs with the wind between them."; 9. fallen_star -- ours: "Fallen Star" -- Star then Ember then Storm on weapon -- hint: "The star falls, burns, and splits the sky."; 10. mirror_of_nothing -- ours: "Mirror of Nothing" -- Void then Stone on wear -- hint: "Nothing, held still by stone.". The hint must still point at the runes in that order (by their marks: Edge, Ember, Root, Tide, Stone, Fortune, Wind, Eye, Storm, Song, Star, Void), short, in his voice.

briefs.title: Beast contracts

briefs.title: Tips the world gives
briefs.ask:
HOW TO WRITE FOR ELIET (Robert, 2026-10-04: "the story and explanations should be easy to understand and be meaningful, or give something more to the game -- either filling out its history or giving hints and tips through conversation, reading, secrets, treasure and inheritance"). 1. PLAIN WORDS, SHORT SENTENCES: someone reading by torchlight should understand it the first time; most sentences under 20 words; at most one invented name per sentence. 2. EVERY PIECE EARNS ITS PLACE: it tells a real piece of the world's history (who, what happened, why it matters now) or gives a useful hint (where something is hidden, what a thing is for, how to beat or avoid a danger, what a gate or a master wants) -- the best do both. Mood alone is not enough. 3. HINTS ARE TRUE: only hint at what you've been told is there; never invent a rule of the world. 4. SAY IT AS SOMEONE IN THE WORLD WOULD: a miner's warning, a dead master's advice, a note left in a chest; concrete names, places and numbers beat moods. 5. CONNECT IT: name what the world already has -- Eliet, Elder Mo, Smith Hale, Apothecary Lin, Trader Wen, Captain Rhee and the Lodge, the first expedition forty years ago (nine went down, one came back), the Jade Pagoda, Shellhaven on the sleeping tortoise, the Mirror on floor 25, the Heart at the bottom, the nanites in every child of Eliet -- so the pieces add up to one history.

These are the TIPS the game gives -- true, useful things, found scratched on lore stones, inside hidden walls, in chests, in a dead master's last words, and from anyone asked for advice. The game fills each {placeholder} with the real thing (a number, a floor, an item, a name). Rewrite each in the voice of the world -- plainer and warmer than ours if you can, never longer than two sentences -- keeping EVERY placeholder exactly as written. In this order (set "id" exactly): secrets -- ours: "There are still {n} hidden ways on this floor. Look for a stone that sits wrong in the wall, and push it." -- keep exactly these: {n}; hidden_chest -- ours: "Something on this floor only shows itself to those who can sense it. Stand still, open your senses, and look again."; gate -- ours: "The stairs down to floor {floor} won't let you pass without {needs}." -- keep exactly these: {floor} {needs}; gate_item -- ours: "{item} is made from {mats}. Make it before you go down -- it's spent at the gate." -- keep exactly these: {item} {mats}; material -- ours: "That {item} you're carrying is wanted for {made}." -- keep exactly these: {item} {made}; boss -- ours: "The master of this floor is {boss}. When it winds up a heavy blow, raise your guard just as it lands: it staggers, and it's yours for a moment." -- keep exactly these: {boss}; master -- ours: "{rumour}" -- keep exactly these: {rumour}; craft -- ours: "{rumour}" -- keep exactly these: {rumour}; cleanse -- ours: "Sit with Cleanse as your focus and the meridians wash clean, node by node. Every clean node makes you a little stronger for good."; clash -- ours: "{a} and {b} are fighting inside you. Let one grow well past the other, or feed {c}, which sits between them." -- keep exactly these: {a} {b} {c}; research -- ours: "The swarm in your blood can be taught. Sit with Research as your focus, and it learns what you choose."; friend -- ours: "{name} thinks well of you. Ask, and they might travel with you." -- keep exactly these: {name}; sitting -- ours: "Qi comes twice as fast at a shrine. Sit where the old stones are, when you can."; parry -- ours: "Raise your guard at the last moment and a blow is parried, not just blocked: it hurts them, not you.". NEW (round 45) -- the world's news, said as advice: camp_unmet -- ours: "People live down on floor {floor} -- a whole camp of them. Find them. A friend that deep is worth having." camp_need -- ours: "{camp}, on floor {floor}, needs help today: {need}" market -- ours: "{trader} is up in Eliet today, selling things from the deep you can't get anywhere else." festival -- ours: "The {name} is in {days}. Be in Eliet for it: the traders give a little off, and the elder has a gift for anyone who walks the deep." hunters -- ours: "The Hollow Clans have hunters out for you. Pay tribute at one of their camps -- the Gnawed Banner on floor 12 is nearest -- and they'll stop." (relic and season are filled in whole; leave them.) NEW (round 46: hidden traps and secrets): traps -- ours: "Someone set plates in the floors down here. Watch for a few loose pebbles or a darker stone, and stop to look before you cross a quiet room. If you hear a click, roll." And secrets is now -- ours: "This floor still hides {n} way through its walls -- maybe more. Stand still beside a wall and feel for a draft. Where the air moves, a stone will give." Keep the hint about the draft.

briefs.title: The history of Eliet, in pieces
briefs.ask:
HOW TO WRITE FOR ELIET (Robert, 2026-10-04: "the story and explanations should be easy to understand and be meaningful, or give something more to the game -- either filling out its history or giving hints and tips through conversation, reading, secrets, treasure and inheritance"). 1. PLAIN WORDS, SHORT SENTENCES: someone reading by torchlight should understand it the first time; most sentences under 20 words; at most one invented name per sentence. 2. EVERY PIECE EARNS ITS PLACE: it tells a real piece of the world's history (who, what happened, why it matters now) or gives a useful hint (where something is hidden, what a thing is for, how to beat or avoid a danger, what a gate or a master wants) -- the best do both. Mood alone is not enough. 3. HINTS ARE TRUE: only hint at what you've been told is there; never invent a rule of the world. 4. SAY IT AS SOMEONE IN THE WORLD WOULD: a miner's warning, a dead master's advice, a note left in a chest; concrete names, places and numbers beat moods. 5. CONNECT IT: name what the world already has -- Eliet, Elder Mo, Smith Hale, Apothecary Lin, Trader Wen, Captain Rhee and the Lodge, the first expedition forty years ago (nine went down, one came back), the Jade Pagoda, Shellhaven on the sleeping tortoise, the Mirror on floor 25, the Heart at the bottom, the nanites in every child of Eliet -- so the pieces add up to one history.

Write one more FRAGMENT of the history of Eliet and the deep -- found one at a time on lore stones and in hidden places, unlocked by how deep the reader has been. What's already known (do not repeat it, build on it): How Eliet began (from floor 0): Eliet was a mining camp before it was a village. The first families came for the jade in the hills, and stayed because the valley was quiet. Nobody dug deep. Nobody needed to.; The shaft under the well (from floor 1): The shaft was found when the old well went dry. Someone climbed down to see why, and found stairs cut into the rock below the water line. Nobody in Eliet had cut them.; Who made the gates (from floor 3): The iron gates and chests in the deep are older than Eliet. Smith Hale says the cut is too clean for goblins and too strange for people. The deep made them, he says -- the way a tree makes bark.; The mine on floor six (from floor 6): Forty years ago men came to Eliet buying ore. Trader Wen sold them forty crates. They used it to sink a mine shaft on floor six, and the village never asked what they were digging for.; The first expedition (from floor 8): Nine people went down the shaft forty years ago, to find where the ore came from. They were the first to pass floor ten. Only one came back, and he never said what he saw.; What the children carry (from floor 10): Every child born in Eliet in the last forty years carries nanites in the blood. Apothecary Lin can see them under glass. Before the expedition came back, no one in the village had them.; Why the Lodge keeps a book (from floor 11): Captain Rhee's Lodge writes down every floor anyone reaches, and who reached it. It began as a list of the dead from the first expedition. Now it's a list of records, and people want their names in it.; Why the sects watch Eliet (from floor 12): The sects in the hills don't care about villages. They care about the shaft. A cultivator who comes back from floor ten carries more qi than most of their disciples, and every sect wants that cultivator in its hall.; The town on the tortoise (from floor 15): Shellhaven is built on the back of a tortoise that has slept for longer than anyone remembers. The people there came down from Eliet a generation ago, and never went back up. They say the tortoise keeps the deep calm.; The Jade Pagoda (from floor 21): The first expedition reached a pagoda of green jade around the twentieth floor. Eight of the nine died beyond it. Elder Mo was the one who came back. He has kept that secret for forty years.; The ninth man (from floor 44): The ninth member of the first expedition was Trader Wen's grandfather. Wen never knew. His grandfather left a sealed letter, to be opened only if his seal was ever found below.; The Mirror (from floor 25): On the twenty-fifth floor the deep shows each traveller themselves. Mo says that's what the deep is now: a mirror of whoever goes deepest. Past the Mirror, no one had made a map until you.; What the nanites were for (from floor 27): The nanites were made for one thing: to bridge a cultivator to the heavens -- a ladder of machines where there should have been a path. The ladder never reached. Everything else they do, they learned while trying.; Why the children get sick (from floor 40): Every floor someone takes, the deep reaches a little further up into everyone who carries it. The children feel it first. Lin's draught dulls it. Nothing has cured it.; The star iron door (from floor 38): Forty years ago someone locked a door of star iron from the far side, around the fortieth floor. Mo thinks it was one of the first expedition, sealing the deep behind them. Whoever it was never came back to open it.; The Heart of the Deep (from floor 45): At the bottom of the shaft something beats. The old stones call it the Heart. Every nanite in Eliet came from it, and every one of them still answers to it.. Each new fragment: a short title, the floor from which it can be found (a fragment about something deep must not be found shallower than that), and 2-4 plain sentences that add something new and true to this history -- a person, an event, a reason -- which makes the rest make more sense. No new mysteries without an answer somewhere.

briefs.title: The five peoples

The five peoples of the world. Each description is shown on the World page next to the player's standing. briefs.ask: Write plainly (the principles at the top of the writing room): short sentences, real names from Eliet's history, and every line must give the player something -- a piece of history or a true hint. Camps of real people living on the dungeon floors. The headman says this the first time you meet them. briefs.title: Names for the game's music (shown for a moment when a piece starts)
briefs.ask: Write plainly. Each piece of the game's music gets a short title, shown for a few seconds in a corner when it starts playing, like a song on a record. Two to five words, the way a musician in this world would name a tune: a place, a time of day, a feeling, a thing you'd see -- no game words, no numbers. Set "id" exactly and put the title in "text": village_1 -- the village by day, warm, flute and zither | village_2 -- the village by day, unhurried, zither first | village_3 -- the village by day, the fiddle (erhu) singing | village_night_1 -- the village at night, a low bamboo flute | village_night_2 -- the village at night, zither and bells | valley_1 -- the valley of the sects, wide and airy | valley_2 -- the valley, bright, bells over the zither | valley_3 -- the valley, a low flute, calm | dungeon_1 -- the upper dungeon, wary, minor | dungeon_2 -- the upper dungeon, the fiddle, a slow drum | dungeon_3 -- the upper dungeon, very quiet, bells | deep_1 -- the deep (floors 10-29), dark, fiddle and bells, ends on a gong | deep_2 -- the deep, a low flute over a slow drum | deep_3 -- the deep, the zither alone in the dark | abyss_1 -- the abyss (floors 30-50), old instruments over the swarm's cold machines | abyss_2 -- the abyss, the fiddle and the machines, ends on a gong | haven_1 -- a town in the deep, a little warmth underground | haven_2 -- a town in the deep, a flute by the hearth | title_1 -- the title screen

briefs.title: How to read a foe: the tell before each kind of attack
briefs.ask: Write plainly. In a fight every dangerous move is shown before it lands, so a watchful player can step aside, guard or parry. For each move below write ONE or TWO short sentences an old fighter would tell a newcomer: what you SEE (or hear) just before it, and what to DO. True to the move as described, no numbers, no game words. Set "id" exactly and put the words in "text": brawler -- a plain fighter; its heavy blow: it draws back and its weapon flashes red for a moment, then swings; step back or parry | charger -- lowers its head, a warning ring shows where it starts, then it runs in a straight line at where you WERE; step sideways | ranged -- holds still and its orb glows brighter, then fires a bolt you can see; sidestep it, or guard | guardian -- carries a shield that stops blades from the front; get behind it, or use arts | skulker -- unseen until close, its first strike hits hardest; slow down near shadows, spirit sense finds it | swarmer -- comes with its young; the young are weak, the mother calls more if left alone | mender -- heals the others with a green glow; kill it first | thunderous -- an elite that raises its arms, a ring spreads on the ground, then it stomps; get out of the ring | venomous -- its strikes poison you (it never kills, but it wears you down); cleanse or rest | vampiric -- heals itself on every hit; burst it down, don't trade blows | splitting -- breaks into smaller copies when it falls; keep your back clear | warding -- a ward shimmers around it and takes the first hits; arts break wards | frenzied -- gets faster as it's hurt; finish it quickly | boss_enrage -- a master at half its health turns red and roars, and strikes faster; pull back for a breath, then press | boss_slam -- a master leaps and lands where you stand, a shadow grows there first; move | boss_sweep -- a master spins with its weapon out, a wide ring shows the reach; get out or guard

briefs.title: What the deep says when you clear a floor (by how well you did)
briefs.ask: Write plainly. When the player finishes a floor (the master beaten or the floor explored), a short card shows how they did, graded S, A, B, C or D, from time, what they found, how much they explored and how close they came to falling. For each grade write a TITLE (two to four words) and ONE short line, as if an old cultivator watching from somewhere were judging them -- dry, a little warm, never cruel; S is rare and should feel earned; D is gentle and points to what to do better. Three of each, so the player doesn't see the same one twice in a row. Set "id" exactly and put "Title -- line" in "text": s_1, s_2, s_3 (flawless: fast, thorough, untouched) | a_1, a_2, a_3 (very good) | b_1, b_2, b_3 (solid) | c_1, c_2, c_3 (got through, missed a lot) | d_1, d_2, d_3 (barely made it: nearly fell, saw little)

briefs.title: Little moments while the character works alone (meditating, training, gathering, crafting)
briefs.ask: Write plainly. When the player steps away from the game, their character keeps working at a pursuit, and when they come back a short report reads like a timeline. Write ONE short line (under 20 words) for a small moment that happened in the middle of that work -- something seen, felt or got right; quiet, specific, a little warm; second person ('you'). Never a reward or a number. Set "id" exactly and put the line in "text": m_1, m_2, m_3, m_4 (meditating) | t_1, t_2, t_3, t_4 (training a weapon or art alone) | g_1, g_2, g_3, g_4 (out gathering herbs, ore, fish or game on the floors they know) | c_1, c_2, c_3, c_4 (working at the crafting bench)

briefs.title: Words carved on the waystones
briefs.ask: Write plainly. Every place the player can quick-travel back to has a waystone: a carved standing stone with a band of runes and a ring of light above it, left by travellers of an older age. When the player first touches one, the words carved on it show. Write ONE line each (under 16 words): a traveller's blessing, a warning, a joke left by a tired mason, a name and a promise -- old, plain and human, never grand. Set "id" as w_1 to w_12 and put the line in "text".

briefs.title: Heavenly inheritances: the greatest masters' last words
briefs.ask: Write plainly (the principles at the top of the writing room): short sentences, and every line must give the player something -- who this master was, and a true hint at what their legacy does. These are the HEAVENLY inheritances: only three of the six appear in any one game, deep in the dungeon, and the player must be strong and beat the master's echo in a fight before the legacy is theirs. Each is two or three sentences: what the player SEES (the seated master, one striking detail), then the master's last words in quotes. Set "id" exactly and put the words in "text": jade_sky -- the Jade Sky Emperor; ours: "A figure in white jade robes sits on a lotus of stone, untouched by a single grain of dust. \"Ten thousand years I ruled a heaven that is gone. All I kept was the body that ruled it. Take it -- and stand where nothing can move you.\"" | star_sword -- the Star-Cleaving Sword Ancestor; ours: "An old swordsman sits with no sword at all; the scar of a cut runs across the stone wall behind him and on into the dark. \"I cut a star once. It was the last thing I ever needed to cut. Learn the intent, not the sword.\"" | void_sage -- the Sage Beyond the Void; ours: "There is a seated sage here, and also there isn't: the outline flickers like heat over stone. \"I breathed in the void and it did not end me. Breathe as I did, and the heavens will pour into you.\"" | vermilion_phoenix -- the Undying Vermilion Phoenix; ours: "A woman sits in a ring of cold ash that is still, somehow, warm. \"Nine times I burned and nine times I came back. The tenth time, I chose to stay. Take the fire -- it remembers how to bring you back.\"" | wind_saint -- the Saint Who Walked the Wind; ours: "The seated figure is so light the air moves its sleeves. \"I walked the nine winds from one end of the sky to the other and never once touched the ground. Here -- learn to be where the blow isn't.\"" | first_seed -- the First of the Makers; ours: "Not bones -- a figure of grey metal and jade, seated, its chest open on a single dark seed that still pulses. \"We made the swarm to carry people up the road. Then we forgot why. You remember. Take the seed.\""

briefs.title: Quests: what each person says when they ask for help
briefs.ask: Write plainly (the principles at the top of the writing room): short sentences, real names from Eliet and the deep's towns, and every pitch must make the player WANT to help -- who is asking, what they lost or need, and one concrete detail. Two to four sentences, in the asker's own voice, in quotes. Keep what the quest actually asks for the same (the floor, the thing, the craft, the count); change only how it's said. Set "id" exactly and put the words in "text": lost_brother -- Little Rin asks (The Brother Who Went Down, a side quest); ours: "\"My brother Tam went down the stair with the first expedition. Everyone says he's dead. He promised he'd scratch our sign on a wall if he got past the goblins -- a little fox. Will you look for it?\"" | pells_hammer -- Old Pell asks (Old Pell's Hammer, a side quest); ours: "\"Forty years I swung a hammer in the warrens before they were warrens. Dropped it running from the first goblins. It's got my name burned in the haft. I'd like it back before I die, if it's not too much bother.\"" | lins_cure -- Apothecary Lin asks (A Cure for the Damp Cough, a side quest); ours: "\"Half the village coughs every thaw. The old miners swore by a moss that grows only where the Drowned Seam meets dry stone. Bring me some, and the herbs to bind it, and we'll see if they were right.\"" | rhee_deserter -- Captain Rhee asks (The Deserter, a side quest); ours: "\"One of my scouts, Joss, ran from the Sanctum and never came back up. If he's alive he's a deserter, and the law says I bring him in. If he's dead, I want his tag. Find out which.\"" | fen_lost_load -- Fen the Porter asks (Fen's Lost Load, a side quest); ours: "\"I carry for everyone in Shellhaven. Last trip down to the Grove, the vines took me by the ankle and I dropped the lot. Three bundles. Shellhaven goes hungry without them.\"" | kesh_son -- Mother Kesh asks (Mother Kesh's Son, a side quest); ours: "\"My boy Dov went to the Ember Forges to learn smithing from the dead. That was a month ago. The forges don't give back what they take, they say. Prove them wrong.\"" | barrow_names -- Ysolde asks (The Names in the Clay, a side quest); ours: "\"The terracotta soldiers on Floor 8 each had a name pressed into the clay. My grandmother's family is down there. I want their names -- five tablets -- so someone remembers.\"" | sword_grave_oath -- Warden Tolle asks (An Oath at the Sword Grave, a side quest); ours: "\"Every warden of Shellhaven swore an oath at the Sword Grave. The oath-stone was broken by something big. Nobody's sworn since. Clear the way, and bring me a shard of the stone.\"" | ilse_ferry -- Ferrywoman Ilse asks (The Last Ferry, a side quest); ours: "\"My ferry ran to the Drowned Palace before the water rose. The palace bell still rings down there, they say, when no one's pulling it. Ring it three times and the old ferry-spirits lead the drowned home. Will you?\"" | corin_debt -- Corin Ashwake asks (Corin's Debt, a side quest); ours: "\"I owe the Hollow Clans for a beast I lost. Their hunter, Red-Mane, says I pay in blood or in pelts. Bring me four pelts from the Crimson Canopy, and I live.\"" | cloud_palace_letters -- Lanternwright Agna asks (Letters from the Cloud Palace, a side quest); ours: "\"My great-grandfather was a clerk in the Fallen Cloud Palace when it fell. He wrote to his wife every day. She never got them. They're still in his desk, I'd bet. Four letters is all I ask.\"" | spore_cure -- Wren of the Salt-Pills asks (Spore-Lung, a side quest); ours: "\"Three of our divers came back from the Spore-Choked Deeps coughing green. I can make a cure, but only from the heart of a spore-mother. And I need you to brew the base yourself -- my hands shake now.\"" | thunder_rods -- Inge Copperhand asks (Lightning in a Rod, a side quest); ours: "\"Ironroot's forges run on stolen lightning -- copper rods we planted at the top of the Thunderhead Spire. The storm-things tore three of them down. Plant new ones.\"" | dragon_scale -- Brokk Ashenbeard asks (A Scale from the Sleeping Dragon, a side quest); ours: "\"They say the Spine of the Sleeping Dragon is just rock that looks like a dragon. I say it's a dragon. Bring me a scale from its spine and I'll eat my beard.\"" | star_iron_find -- Marn Two-Picks asks (The Miner's Last Seam, a side quest); ours: "\"My partner died in the Fallen Star Mine, but not before he found a seam of star iron so pure it sang. He marked the way with chalk. Follow his chalk, finish his work, and the ore's half yours.\"" | bell_of_yao -- Yao the Bellringer asks (The Bellringer's Missing Notes, a side quest); ours: "\"The Pagoda's great bell has nine notes. Thieves took three of the striking-stones to the Clockwork Vaults to make their machines tick. Without them the bell is a cripple.\"" | weavers_silk -- Lady Xiu asks (Silk for the Lady, a side quest); ours: "\"The Weaver's Halls spin a silk that turns a blade. The weavers are not kind about sharing. Bring me their queen's spinneret, and I'll make you a robe fit for the Pagoda.\"" | archive_index -- Elder Bai asks (The Lost Index, a side quest); ours: "\"The Frozen Archive holds every technique the old sects ever wrote down. Useless without the index -- six ice-sealed codex keys. Find them, and the Pagoda's library will open its back shelves to you.\"" | mirror_twin -- Disciple Rou asks (The Disciple in the Mirror, a side quest); ours: "\"My twin walked into the Mirror Labyrinth and a copy of her walked out. It smiles wrong. The real one's still in there, I know it. Find her -- and find the thing wearing her face.\"" | night_market -- Lin Jade-Hand asks (A Debt at the Night Market, a side quest); ours: "\"I bought something at the Night Market of the Dead. Thieves took it to the Glass Dunes to sell. Mend it -- I'll teach you the tuning words.\"" | cinder_duel -- Ves Flame-Tongue asks (A Duel for Ves, a side quest); ours: "\"The storm-king of the Stormbreak Stair burned my brother to ash and calls it a duel won. Answer for me.\"" | silent_bells -- Old Mother Silence asks (The Bells of Silence, a side quest); ours: "\"Our order keeps silence because the Deep listens. But the shrines on the way are dark. Light them for me, three of them, and I'll walk the rest myself.\"" | abbot_doubt -- Abbot Lune asks (The Abbot's Doubt, a side quest); ours: "\"I have kept this monastery sixty years believing the Heart of the Deep is holy. A brother came back from the Cooling Dunes and said it is only hungry. Bring me what he saw: the carving at the dune's heart.\"" | smith_1 -- Smith Hale asks (The Apprentice's Anvil, a blacksmithing quest); ours: "\"You want to swing a sword, you ought to know what's in one. The good ones use star iron from the Fallen Star Mine. Bring some up and make yours.\"" | smith_5 -- Yao the Bellringer asks (A Blade Worth a Bell, a blacksmithing quest); ours: "\"I cast bells. Make me a Masterwork -- anything -- and I'll tell you the secret of the temper that makes both.\"" | smith_6 -- Bryn Feather asks (Forged in Firebird Flame, a blacksmithing quest); ours: "\"The Nest's forge burns on a firebird's breath. Only a grandmaster may work it. Make eight pieces at the grandmaster's pace and one Masterwork from the deep's own metal, and the flame is yours to use.\"" | alch_1 -- Apothecary Lin asks (First Fire, an alchemy quest); ours: "\"Alchemy starts with incense and patience. Burn me a stick of qi incense, then three qi pills -- and don't blow up my shop.\"" | alch_2 -- Lio of the Seven Jars asks (The Seven Jars, an alchemy quest); ours: "\"Seven jars, seven roots, seven fires. You've learned one. Bring me ember root and iron thistle from below, and brew me an ember pill and a thistle pill.\"" | alch_3 -- Wren of the Salt-Pills asks (Salt and Breath, an alchemy quest); ours: "\"Divers need breath more than courage. Brew me a deep breath pill, and then brew anything well -- Fine or better. I want to see care, not luck.\"" | alch_4 -- Pell Ironroot asks (Earthmarrow, an alchemy quest); ours: "\"Ironroot alchemy is slow alchemy. The earthmarrow pill takes the deep's own patience. Show me five brews and one earthmarrow.\"" | alch_5 -- Sister Qing asks (The Pagoda's Elixir, an alchemy quest); ours: "\"The heartfire elixir is the Pagoda's pride. Brew one, and brew something Superior, and I will put your name in the furnace-book.\"" | alch_6 -- Ruan Cinderfall asks (The Ash Pill, an alchemy quest); ours: "\"Every grandmaster makes one Masterwork pill and eats it in front of their teacher. Bone broth puts colour back in a face. Make me three pots and I'll feed the whole shift.\"" | med_3 -- Sister Lumiara asks (Resin and Rest, a medicine quest); ours: "\"Pilgrims arrive here with their feet in ribbons. The old resin salve heals in a night, but nobody here can make it any more. Can you?\"" | jewel_1 -- Cassiel Vane asks (A Lucky Charm, a jewelcrafting quest); ours: "\"Sailors buy luck before they buy rope. Cut me two lucky charms and I'll sell them by evening -- and pay you more than they're worth.\"" | jewel_2 -- Lin Jade-Hand asks (Jade for Jade-Hand, a jewelcrafting quest); ours: "\"They call me Jade-Hand because I can tell real jade from glass blind. Can you cut it? Make me a jade ring, and something of Fine quality.\"" | jewel_3 -- Sigrid Lamplow asks (The Emperor's Pendant, a jewelcrafting quest); ours: "\"An old buyer wants an emperor-jade pendant. Nobody in Ironroot can cut one. If you can, you'll be the only jeweller below Lanternmere worth the name.\"" | gath_1 -- Trader Wen asks (Pick of the Warrens, a gathering quest); ours: "\"Herbs and ore -- that's what moves in Eliet. Bring me a good haul from below and I'll pay you a fair price and a little more.\"" | gath_2 -- Thora asks (Ore for the Smelters, a gathering quest); ours: "\"The smelters are cold. Twelve veins' worth of ore and they'll run all winter.\"" | gath_3 -- Brin Saltfoot asks (Saltwater Fishing, a gathering quest); ours: "\"The lake's full of blind fish that taste like the sky. The healers say moonpetal tea. I can't go down there. Please? Six flowers.\"" | gath_6 -- Ottilie Warm asks (A Garden in the Nest, a gathering quest); ours: "\"Nothing grows in the Nest -- too hot. But you've a garden up top, they say. Grow something and bring me the seed of it.\"" | soc_1 -- Trader Wen asks (Old Grudges, a quest about people); ours: "\"Smith Hale and I haven't spoken in nine years. Over a pot. A POT. Talk to him, would you? I'm too proud and so is he.\"" | soc_2 -- Little Rin asks (Rin's Friend, a quest about people); ours: "\"Everyone in the village is old. Will you be my friend? A real one -- you have to come and talk to me, not just pass by.\"" | soc_3 -- Hollin Brask asks (A Night at the Brask, a quest about people); ours: "\"An innkeeper hears everything. Shellhaven's friendlier than it looks -- you just have to sit down.\"" | soc_4 -- Mother Orla asks (The Matchmaker, a quest about people); ours: "\"Captain Vey and the lampkeeper have been making eyes at each other for two years and neither will say a word. My sister was Elder Mo's wife. Take him a letter for me -- I haven't the courage to go up the stair.\"" | mast_1 -- Captain Rhee asks (Rhee's Drill, a master's training); ours: "\"My scouts live because they don't get hit. Roll through fifteen blows, and turn five aside with your guard at the last instant. Then we'll talk.\"" | mast_2 -- Circle-Keeper Venn asks (The Breaking Stance, a master's training); ours: "\"Strength is nothing. Breaking is everything. Stagger ten foes -- wear their balance down until they reel -- and I'll show you where to stand.\"" | mast_3 -- Captain Vey asks (The Elite Hunter, a master's training); ours: "\"Any fool kills goblins. The marked ones -- the elites, the ones that glow -- those are a hunter's work. Five of them.\"" | mast_4 -- Kettil Moss asks (Sit Like Stone, a master's training); ours: "\"The moss grows on the stone because the stone sits still. Open three points of your meridian lattice by sitting. Then sit with me.\"" | mast_5 -- Master Ou asks (The Ninefold Form, a master's training); ours: "\"An art you only know is a tool. An art you've grown is a limb. Grow your arts -- three new stages of mastery -- and I'll teach you the form that joins them.\"" | mast_6 -- Old Kael asks (The Old Way, a master's training); ours: "\"Floor masters. The great ones. Kill two -- properly, face to face -- and an old man will tell you how he lived so long.\"" | mast_7 -- Sister Hush asks (The Silent Strike, a master's training); ours: "(Sister Hush writes on a slate: \"Thirty in the Black Canopy. Thin them out. Fifteen.\"" | exp_1 -- Tamsin the Lamplighter asks (Light the Way Down, an exploration quest); ours: "\"Every secret door you find, I mark on my map so the next walker doesn't miss it. Get down to the Mirror Labyrinth, and see three of the deep's great sights along the way, and I'll sell good ones.\"" | exp_4 -- Sister Pale asks (To the Bottom, an exploration quest); ours: "\"No one from this monastery has seen the Heart and come back to describe it. Go to the last floor before it and tell me what the air is like.\"" | iron_fist_clan_1 -- Master Wei asks (Iron in the Blood, a sect quest); ours: "Master Wei looks at your hands before your face. \"Soft. Bring me five lumps of iron from below, and put one of the valley's strutting disciples on his back. Then we'll talk about whether you're worth a trial.\"" | iron_fist_clan_2 -- Master Wei asks (The Hundred Blows, a sect quest); ours: "\"Outer disciples are hammers that haven't been struck yet. Then tell Lan you're done -- she keeps the count.\"" | iron_fist_clan_3 -- Master Wei asks (The Broken Gauntlet, a sect quest); ours: "Wei doesn't look up. \"Disciple Hu went to the Sword Grave to prove he could take a blade from it. Gather more of what grows. Clear a tower floor without breaking. Disciple Mei will tell me if you've learned anything.\"" | whispering_willow_3 -- Master Hu asks (The Strangled Grove, a sect quest); ours: "\"Below us, a grove has gone wrong. The Strangling Grove. Bring Disciple Shen the cutting's last seed, and decide with him what we do.\"" | whispering_willow_4 -- Master Hu asks (The First Willow, a sect quest); ours: "\"Every willow in the grove came from one tree, and that tree grew in the Crimson Canopy before the canopy turned red. A cutting of it still lives -- I've dreamed it. You're Core now. The tea will be fresh.\"" | misty_peak_monastery_2 -- Master Ling asks (Rain in the Bowl, a sect quest); ours: "\"Water takes the shape of what holds it. So will you. Catch three fish from the deep's waters. Read three more stones. Clear two floors of a tower without hurrying. Then show Disciple Bao your bowl.\"" | misty_peak_monastery_3 -- Master Ling asks (The Drowned Bell, a sect quest); ours: "\"Our monastery had a bell, once. The flood that made the Drowned Palace took it down with the palace. Disciple Ren says he hears it at night. I think Ren is right. Find it -- and whatever has been ringing it.\"" | misty_peak_monastery_4 -- Master Ling asks (The Tide-Mirror, a sect quest); ours: "\"The first abbot kept a mirror of still water that never spilled. She carried it into the Singing Crystal Caverns to listen to the deep, and the caverns kept her. You are Core now. Bring the mirror home.\"" | misty_peak_monastery_5 -- Master Ling asks (Ten Thousand Rivers, a sect quest); ours: "\"All rivers come back to the sea. Climb a tower to its top. Win five bouts without anger. Then go to the Tidewrecked Court, where the flood began, and end it. Come back and tell me where you'll flow next.\"" | stoneheart_brotherhood_1 -- Master Shen asks (Behind the Waterfall, a sect quest); ours: "Master Shen has to shout over the waterfall. \"You found the caves! Most don't. Now find out if you last. Twenty kills in the deep, and get down to the Nanite Sanctum. Then come back through the water.\"" | stoneheart_brotherhood_2 -- Master Shen asks (Weight of the Mountain, a sect quest); ours: "\"A brother carries. Bring the stores two good stones from the deep -- jade, if you can find it. Put forty more foes down. Then tell Disciple Qiu, who has carried water up the cave stair every day for nine years.\"" | stoneheart_brotherhood_3 -- Master Shen asks (The Clay Brother, a sect quest); ours: "\"In the Terracotta Barrows there's a clay soldier that wears our mark. Disciple Tao swears it's his grandfather, who went down a hundred years ago and never came up. Find the mark. Find the soldier. Then Tao will need someone beside him.\"" | stoneheart_brotherhood_4 -- Master Shen asks (The First Heartstone, a sect quest); ours: "\"Every brother carries a heartstone. The first one -- the founder's -- is still in the dragon's spine, where he lay down to sleep and never woke. You're Core now. Go and wake him, or at least take his heart home.\"" | stoneheart_brotherhood_5 -- Master Shen asks (The Unmoving Mountain, a sect quest); ours: "\"A mountain doesn't move -- but it's still there when the storm's gone. Summit a tower. Win five bouts. Then go to the Dragon's Ribs, where the dragon's heart is, and stand in front of what lives there. Come back and tell me what you'll be.\"" | silverleaf_grove_1 -- Master Yun asks (Silver Under the Leaves, a sect quest); ours: "Master Yun is older than the trees, and says so. \"Everything that grows teaches, if you're slow enough to learn. Bring me six spirit herbs, picked whole. Not five. Not seven.\"" | silverleaf_grove_2 -- Master Yun asks (The Grove-Keeper's Round, a sect quest); ours: "\"A keeper walks the grove every day and notices what changed. Gather ten more things that grow. See two of the deep's great sights. Then walk the round with Disciple Yan and tell her what you noticed.\"" | silverleaf_grove_3 -- Master Yun asks (Spore and Root, a sect quest); ours: "\"Decay is sacred too. But what's happening in the Spore-Choked Deeps isn't decay -- it's hunger. Disciple Zhi has been studying it. Bring back a sample of the mother-spore, and end the thing that grows it. Zhi will know what to do with it. Or think he will.\"" | silverleaf_grove_4 -- Master Yun asks (Seed of the Elder Tree, a sect quest); ours: "\"The grove's elder tree spun its seeds into silk, and the silk was stolen by a weaver in the deep. The Weaver's Halls. You're Core -- you'll know a stolen thing when you see it. Bring one seed home.\"" | silverleaf_grove_5 -- Master Yun asks (Wisdom of the Ages, a sect quest); ours: "\"I'm older than the trees, I said. Not older than what's below. Summit a tower. Read five of the old stones. Then go to the Rotting Bloom, where the hunger started, and end it for good. Then tell me what you'll keep.\"" | crimson_veil_1 -- Master Xi asks (A Candle in the Wind, a sect quest); ours: "Master Xi lights a candle and hands it to you in the wind off the red lake. It doesn't go out. \"Good. Bring me ember root from below, and kill one of the deep's marked things -- the ones that glow. Fire knows fire.\"" | crimson_veil_2 -- Master Xi asks (Through the Braziers, a sect quest); ours: "\"The crucible is where the weak burns off. Put down three of the marked ones. Win two bouts. Bring the stores five more ember roots. Then walk the ring of braziers with Disciple Ping and don't flinch.\"" | crimson_veil_3 -- Master Xi asks (The Forge That Went Cold, a sect quest); ours: "\"Disciple Wen's family kept a forge in the Ember Forges -- until something drank the fire out of it. Bring Wen the forge's last coal, and kill the thing that's drinking. Then help Wen decide what to do with a cold forge.\"" | crimson_veil_4 -- Master Xi asks (The Red Lake's Brazier, a sect quest); ours: "\"The lake below our cliff is red because of what was poured into it: the founder's brazier, thrown down so no one else could have it. It washed down into the deep, into the Ash Dunes. You're Core. Bring it back up.\"" | crimson_veil_5 -- Master Xi asks (Burned Away, Forged Anew, a sect quest); ours: "\"The last trial of the Veil is to burn. Summit a tower. Put down five more of the marked ones. Then go into the Ember Nest, where the firebirds are born, and walk out again. Then tell me what you've become.\"" | concord_1 -- Elder Bai asks (Six Banners, One Valley, a sect quest); ours: "\"Six sects in one valley, and they've not sat at one table in forty years. The Pagoda wants to host a council. Carry my invitations -- Iron Fist, Crimson Veil and Misty Peak first; the rest will follow if those three come.\"" | concord_2 -- Lady Xiu asks (The Grand Tournament of Six Sects, a sect quest); ours: "\"A council needs a tournament -- something to fight about that isn't each other. Win five bouts on the valley road and climb three tower floors, and you'll stand for the Pagoda in the final.\"" | concord_3 -- Elder Bai asks (The Oathbreaker of the Ninth Tier, a sect quest); ours: "\"Forty years ago the sects swore a covenant on the Pagoda's ninth tier. One of the signers broke it, took the covenant scroll and fled into the Frozen Archive. If the council is going to mean anything, we need that scroll -- and someone has to decide what to do with it.\"" | moon_1 -- Sister Hush asks (What the Moon Forgot, a sect quest); ours: "\"The monastery's history was written on three pages that the archive below swallowed. Without them we don't know why we keep the vigil -- only that we do. Find the pages.\"" | moon_2 -- Old Mother Silence asks (The Silent Lesson, a sect quest); ours: "(Old Mother Silence doesn't speak. She points at the old stones on the wall, then at a riddle-stone, then at you, then at her own eyes.)" | moon_3 -- Abbot Lune asks (Moon Over the Abyss, a sect quest); ours: "\"The pages say the first abbot carried a mirror that showed the moon even underground -- and that something below ate the moon out of it. It's in the Starless Pit. Bring it back, and the monastery will have its moon again.\""

briefs.title: The deep's reaches: the ten lands past every floor's edge
briefs.ask: Write plainly (the principles at the top of the writing room). Past the edge of every floor of the deep there is a REACH: a wide natural land of its own, joined by a tunnel through the rock, with a warden guarding its heart. For each land below write ONE description of two sentences that a player reads the first time they walk in: what they see, hear or feel, one concrete detail, no big words. Keep each land what it is (a lake stays a lake, fire stays fire). Set "id" exactly and put the words in "text": crystal -- name: "The Crystal Hollows" | warden: "the Prism Warden" | ours: "Crystal grows out of every wall here, in spears and clusters, and hums when you walk past. The light comes from inside the stone." | emberrift -- name: "The Ember Rift" | warden: "the Rift-Born" | ours: "The rock splits open on rivers of slow fire. Black stone pillars, cracked and glowing, hold the roof up. The heat makes the air shake." | frostgallery -- name: "The Frost Gallery" | warden: "the Rime Sovereign" | ours: "Cold air pours down from somewhere above. Pools have frozen solid, columns of ice stand where water once fell, and snow drifts down out of the dark." | glowcap -- name: "The Glowcap Wood" | warden: "the Glowcap Matriarch" | ours: "Mushrooms as tall as houses, their caps lit from inside. The air is thick and sweet and full of slow green motes." | oldworkings -- name: "The Old Workings" | warden: "the Foreman in the Dark" | ours: "Somebody mined here for generations, then left in a hurry: props and carts, rails into the dark, seams still glittering in the walls." | ossuary -- name: "The Ossuary Fields" | warden: "the Ossuary Keeper" | ours: "Every one of the deep's dead seems to have been carried here and laid down. Skulls in niches, bones in drifts, statues no one remembers." | rootcathedral -- name: "The Root Cathedral" | warden: "the Rootbound Ancient" | ours: "The roots of something enormous on the surface have broken through the roof and grown down in arches. Pale light leaks through where they came in." | stormchasm -- name: "The Storm Chasm" | warden: "the Chasm Stormcaller" | ours: "Lightning lives down here. It crawls over tall black spires and leaves the air sharp and blue; the floor is scorched in branching patterns." | sunkencity -- name: "The Sunken Street" | warden: "the Last Watchman" | ours: "A whole street of some old city, swallowed into the rock: broken columns, toppled statues, flagstones worn by feet a thousand years gone." | underlake -- name: "The Underlake" | warden: "the Thing Under the Water" | ours: "A black lake under the rock, so still it holds the cave's lights twice. Old stone causeways run from island to island."

principles: HOW TO WRITE FOR ELIET (Robert, 2026-10-04: "the story and explanations should be easy to understand and be meaningful, or give something more to the game -- either filling out its history or giving hints and tips through conversation, reading, secrets, treasure and inheritance"). 1. PLAIN WORDS, SHORT SENTENCES: someone reading by torchlight should understand it the first time; most sentences under 20 words; at most one invented name per sentence. 2. EVERY PIECE EARNS ITS PLACE: it tells a real piece of the world's history (who, what happened, why it matters now) or gives a useful hint (where something is hidden, what a thing is for, how to beat or avoid a danger, what a gate or a master wants) -- the best do both. Mood alone is not enough. 3. HINTS ARE TRUE: only hint at what you've been told is there; never invent a rule of the world. 4. SAY IT AS SOMEONE IN THE WORLD WOULD: a miner's warning, a dead master's advice, a note left in a chest; concrete names, places and numbers beat moods. 5. CONNECT IT: name what the world already has -- Eliet, Elder Mo, Smith Hale, Apothecary Lin, Trader Wen, Captain Rhee and the Lodge, the first expedition forty years ago (nine went down, one came back), the Jade Pagoda, Shellhaven on the sleeping tortoise, the Mirror on floor 25, the Heart at the bottom, the nanites in every child of Eliet -- so the pieces add up to one history.
